headline: President Bush created a federal board to focus on protecting Americans' civil liberties.
what_it_does: This executive order set up a new group called the President's Board on Safeguarding Americans' Civil Liberties. Based on its title, the board's job relates to protecting the legal rights and freedoms of people in the United States. No summary was provided, so details about who sits on the board, what powers it has, and how it works are not covered here.

who_it_affects.how: Agencies may be asked to work with or report to the new board on civil liberties matters.
The board's stated purpose is to look out for their civil liberties, though the order's specific effects are not described in the source.
